title: Listening to Manuel Perez and George Moret as a boy
summary: Albert names Manuel Perez and George Moret as the players he listened to, followed in parades and heard at West End. He explains the loose family ties.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Well, who did you listen to come?

Well, Manuel Perez lived across the street from my grandfather, and he was part of the family. And there was another old trumpet player that I very seldom hear too much said about, George Moret. And his wife practically helped my mother to bring me up because that's how close-knit all families were here. All of the Creole families down in this area, they're close-knit. And half the time, my mother couldn't find me. I was either at Old Man Jaws Bowl by my grandfather, by Manuel Perez, all over to Bonnie's house, with Bonnie Bigel, who was his first cousin. And I'd be in one of those places. And you asked me who did I listen to. Well, I used to go out to West End long years ago when he had just nothing but dance halls out there to listen to old George Moret play. And also Manuel. I followed Manuel in the parades, and sometimes I walked the parades with him and carried us home.
Were you any kind of Moret or Parade?

Well, not related to Moret, but to true family ties, yes. But I understand that my grandfather claimed a relationship with Manuel Perez, but what it was right now, I can't remember, but it wasn't close enough for me to be associated as a close relative.
